response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.total) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG((s.share - a.avg_share) / a.avg_share) AS avg_relative_diff FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: 'Each customer' means customers that have at least one invoice. Customers with no invoices are not included in the average share.
Revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total. InvoiceLine is not used.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every customer in the Customer table. Customers with no invoices count as a total of 0, which lowers the average share.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.total) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG((s.share - a.avg_share) / a.avg_share) AS avg_relative_diff FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
